title: Tenant isolation is enforced at the ConceptGateway; cross-tenant access is denied, never silently honored
body:
Every generated CRUD controller and the panel runtime funnel data access through `DefaultConceptGateway` over a `ConceptStore`. Isolation is enforced there, and it must be adversarially trustworthy:

- A request that carries an explicit `tenantId` different from the caller's authenticated `ExecutionContext.tenantId()` is rejected outright with `ConceptGatewayAccessDeniedException(code="TENANT_SCOPE_DENIED")`. This covers read, list, save (write), and delete. Forging `tenantId` in the body/path to reach another tenant does not work.
- A request that omits `tenantId` is scoped to the caller's own tenant: a read/list returns only the caller's rows, and a save/delete only ever touches the caller's partition. Cross-tenant rows are invisible, not leaked.
- Both adapter families must behave identically. History shows `InMemoryConceptStore` (`*-inproc`) and the JDBC store (`JdbcBusinessConceptStore` / `persistence-postgres`) have diverged before (isolation bugs #2, #5, #16 were adapter-specific), so the permanent attack suite `com.finalexec.security.TenantIsolationAttackTest` runs the whole matrix under BOTH, in the hermetic `test` source set the runtimehost gate runs.

Gotcha found + fixed under LNCH-2: `PanelRuntime.deleteRow` passed `tenantId=null` to the gateway and returned `deleted:true` even when the target row belonged to another tenant (a silent no-op that lied). The fix reads the row in the caller's tenant first and refuses when it is not visible. Lesson for any new data-touching surface: never assume tenant-scoped absence == success; confirm visibility, and let the gateway be the single enforcement point.
